front: What is CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing) in one sentence?
back: One-line: browser-enforced policy — server headers permit another origin to read responses; preflight validates "non-simple" requests — Fetch spec / W3C.

front: Explain the mental model of CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing) (how the system thinks).
back: CORS is not server access control — it stops browser JavaScript on https://evil.com from reading responses from https://api.example.com unless the API explicitly allows it. curl/Postman ignore CORS.

Console: blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' → server didn't echo origin. 4. Credentials flag is true, but Access-Control-Allow-Origin is * → must echo exact origin.

front: Symptom: Works in Postman, fails in browser — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: header X-Custom not allowed — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Method PUT not allowed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing Allow-Methods · Fix: Include verb in preflight response

front: Symptom: Cookie not sent cross-origin — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SameSite; missing credentials · Fix: Client: withCredentials: true; server: Allow-Credentials: true + exact ACAO

front: Symptom: Intermittent after deploy — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Duplicate ACAO headers — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Redirect on preflight — what do you check and fix?

front: Gotcha with CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing): what silently fails?
back: CORS is not authentication. Any client without a browser can call your API. Still require JWT authentication / sessions.

front: When should you NOT use CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing)?
back: Server-to-server calls → no CORS needed. Same-origin SPA + API → serve both from one host or use reverse proxy path (/api → backend). "Fix" CORS by disabling browser security — dev-only Chrome flags don't help users.

front: What is IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) in one sentence?
back: Authorization bug: client supplies object id (URL/body); server checks authentication but not ownership — attacker swaps id and reads/writes someone else's data. Includes auto-increment enumeration.

front: Explain the mental model of IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) (how the system thinks).

back: Confusing with CSRF/XSS — IDOR is missing server AuthZ; CSRF is unwanted action; XSS is script injection (cross-site scripting, XSRF (cross-site request forgery)). Rate limiting as fix — slows enumeration, doesn't fix authorization.

front: What is JWT authentication in one sentence?
back: One-line: signed (or encrypted) JSON claims for stateless auth — verify algorithm, signature, and claims server-side every request — RFC 7519.

front: Explain the mental model of JWT authentication (how the system thinks).
back: JWT = header.payload.signature (JWS) or nested JWE. Server trusts token only after cryptographic verification + claim checks. Stateless by default — revocation requires blocklist or short TTL + refresh rotation.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for JWT authentication?
back: Client ── Authorization: Bearer eyJ... ──► API → verify sig (JWKS / shared secret) → check exp, iss, aud, nbf → authorize sub + scopes

front: Given a broken JWT authentication setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Client ── Authorization: Bearer eyJ... ──► API

front: What are the production-safe defaults for JWT authentication?
back: Use jti (unique token ID) for blacklist keys — not the full token string (memory heavy). when user logs in and receives an access token or refresh token, multiple tokens may exist for the same user. jti uniquely identifies each token instance.

front: Symptom: invalid signature after IdP change — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: JWKS kid; cached old key · Fix: Refresh JWKS; support multiple kid; reduce cache TTL during rotation

front: Symptom: jwt expired sporadic — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NTP on API nodes vs IdP · Fix: Sync time (chrony); set clockTolerance: 30

front: Symptom: jwt not active (nbf) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Clock ahead on client · Fix: Fix skew; avoid nbf unless needed

front: Symptom: Auth bypass reports (pen test) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Accept alg: none? HS256 with public key? · Fix: Allowlist algorithms; use asymmetric RS256/ES256 for multi-service

front: Symptom: kid header attack — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: App fetches key from attacker URL via kid path traversal · Fix: Map kid to known JWKS only — never filesystem paths from header

front: Symptom: Logged-out user still works until exp — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No revocation · Fix: Blacklist jti; or short access token (5–15m) + refresh

front: Symptom: Refresh token reuse detected — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Rotation not enforced · Fix: Issue new refresh on use; invalidate family on reuse

front: Symptom: aud mismatch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Token for wrong client · Fix: Validate aud matches your API identifier

front: Gotcha with JWT authentication: what silently fails?
back: alg: none attack: Libraries that honor the header algorithm can accept unsigned tokens if algorithms isn't restricted. Always pass explicit algorithms: ['RS256'].

front: When should you NOT use JWT authentication?
back: Session-heavy monolith with server-side session store already → JWT adds complexity without benefit. Long-lived credentials in mobile apps without secure storage → use platform keystore + refresh rotation. Passing JWT in URL query strings → leaks via logs and Referer.

back: Managed encryption keys — envelope encryption for AWS services and your apps; keys never leave HSM in plaintext. AWS KMS docs + outages when key policy and IAM both had to align.

front: Explain the mental model of KMS (Key Management Service) (how the system thinks).
back: KMS stores Customer Master Keys (CMKs) — symmetric (default) or asymmetric (sign/verify). Data is encrypted with data keys; data keys are wrapped by CMK (envelope encryption). Every use calls kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey — logged in CloudTrail.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for KMS (Key Management Service)?
back: alias/prod-app — human-friendly; rotate underlying CMK with alias re-point (manual or automation). Automatic key rotation (annual) — AWS rotates backing material; same key id, decrypt old ciphertext still works.

front: Symptom: AccessDeniedException on Decrypt — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Key policy and IAM; VPC endpoint? · Fix: Add role to key policy; kms:ViaService conditions

front: Symptom: S3 SSE-KMS upload fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Bucket default encryption key; key policy for S3 · Fix: Allow S3 service principal in key policy

front: Symptom: Lambda/RDS can't read secret — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Secret encrypted with CMK; execution role lacks kms:Decrypt · Fix: Grant role on CMK used by Secrets Manager

front: Symptom: Cross-account Deny — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CMK not shared; external account principal · Fix: Key policy Principal for other account role

front: Symptom: DisabledException — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Key disabled or pending deletion · Fix: Re-enable; cancel deletion window (7–30 days)

front: Symptom: Higher latency — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: KMS API per-object encrypt · Fix: Data key caching (within compliance bounds); batch

front: Gotcha with KMS (Key Management Service): what silently fails?
back: IAM Allow alone is insufficient — CMK key policy must trust the caller (unless account root delegation pattern used correctly).

front: When should you NOT use KMS (Key Management Service)?
back: App-level secrets in env vars without envelope — use Secrets Manager/SSM Parameter Store with KMS CMK. Password hashing — KMS encrypt ≠ bcrypt/Argon2; use for encryption at rest, not password storage. High-frequency per-field encrypt on hot path without cache — cost + latency; batch or use AES-GCM with rotated data keys.

front: What is Token rotation in one sentence?
back: Limit blast radius of leaked credentials — refresh/access tokens, API keys, session ids, and signing keys expire and are replaced on a schedule or after use. RFC 6819 (OAuth 2.0 Threat Model) + prod incidents from never-rotated JWT signing keys.

front: Explain the mental model of Token rotation (how the system thinks).
back: Long-lived secrets will leak (logs, git, browser, support tickets). Rotation means: short TTL + refresh path + revocation/list + key versioning so old material stops working without hard-downtime if done right.

back: Access token (15m) ──► API → Signing keys (JWKS kid) ──► verify old + new during overlap window

back: Access token (15m) ──► API

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Token rotation?
back: Issue with kid in header; verifiers accept both keys for overlap period (e.g. 7 days). Stop signing with old kid; remove from JWKS after max access token TTL elapsed.

front: When should you NOT use Token rotation?
back: Rotate on every API request — unnecessary overhead; match risk (15m access / 7d refresh typical for web). Rotation without revocation store — stolen refresh works until natural expiry if you can't invalidate server-side.

front: What is Single-sign-on (SSO) in one sentence?
back: One-line: one identity provider (IdP) login federates access to many apps via signed assertions — SAML 2.0 or OIDC/OAuth 2.0.

front: Explain the mental model of Single-sign-on (SSO) (how the system thinks).
back: SSO separates authentication (who you are) from app sessions. User authenticates once at the IdP (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Keycloak); the app receives a signed token or assertion and creates a local session.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Single-sign-on (SSO)?
back: User ──► App (SP) ──redirect──► IdP login → App validates signature ──► session cookie / JWT authentication → curl -s https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq . → curl -s https://idp/.well-known/jwks.json | jq . → echo "$ID_TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | jq .

front: Symptom: redirect_uri_mismatch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: IdP app config vs actual callback URL · Fix: Exact match scheme/host/path; trailing slash matters

front: Symptom: invalid_client — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Secret rotated; wrong tenant · Fix: Update client secret; verify tenant ID in issuer URL

front: Symptom: Login works, instant logout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cookie Secure/SameSite; proxy HTTPS · Fix: Terminate TLS at edge; set SameSite=None; Secure if cross-site

front: Symptom: Invalid signature on SAML — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: IdP cert rotated; stale metadata · Fix: Refresh IdP metadata; update SP cert fingerprint

front: Symptom: Audience restriction invalid — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: AuthnStatement too old / skew — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Groups not mapped to roles — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing attribute release · Fix: IdP attribute statement / OIDC groups claim

front: Symptom: Works in dev, fails prod — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Different client IDs; HTTP vs HTTPS · Fix: Separate IdP apps per env; never HTTP callbacks in prod

front: Symptom: Infinite redirect loop — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Session not persisted; cookie domain · Fix: Fix cookie domain; check middleware order

front: Gotcha with Single-sign-on (SSO): what silently fails?
back: Never trust the id_token from the front channel without signature verification against JWKS. Always validate server-side.

front: When should you NOT use Single-sign-on (SSO)?
back: Machine-to-machine APIs → client credentials grant or mTLS, not interactive SSO. Single small app with local users → SSO adds IdP dependency without ROI. Long-lived CLI tools → API keys or device code flow, not browser SSO redirect.

front: What is yescrypt (yashcrypt) in one sentence?
